content: First aid encompasses immediate care provided to injured or ill individuals before professional medical help arrives, potentially preventing condition worsening, promoting recovery, and sometimes saving lives. Effective first aid follows systematic approaches beginning with scene assessment to ensure responder safety and identify hazards before approaching victims. The primary survey follows the ABCDE framework: Airway (checking if the airway is open and clear), Breathing (verifying normal breathing), Circulation (checking pulse and controlling severe bleeding), Disability (assessing responsiveness and neurological status), and Exposure (examining for additional injuries). For unresponsive victims, the recovery positionâplacing them on their side with head tilted back and knees bentâmaintains an open airway and prevents aspiration if vomiting occurs. Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) combines chest compressions and rescue breaths for cardiac arrest victims: compressions should be at least 5 cm deep at a rate of 100-120 per minute, allowing complete chest recoil between compressions. Automated External Defibrillators (AEDs) analyze heart rhythms and deliver shocks to restore normal function in certain types of cardiac arrest. Bleeding control involves direct pressure application to wounds, elevation when appropriate, and pressure points or tourniquets for severe hemorrhage that doesn't respond to direct pressure. Fracture management includes immobilization with splints to prevent movement, aligning limbs in their normal position when possible, and elevating injured extremities to reduce swelling. Burn treatment involves stopping the burning process, cooling the area with cool (not cold) running water for 10-20 minutes, covering with clean, non-stick dressings, and avoiding breaking blisters or applying creams, ointments, or adhesive dressings. Poisoning management varies by substance but generally includes calling poison control, removing the person from danger, and specifically avoiding inducing vomiting unless directed by medical professionals.

scenario.title: Emergency Response Trainer
scenario.content: Students manage first aid scenarios in a virtual sports environment, implementing appropriate care for various injuries and medical emergencies. The simulation presents realistic incidents ranging from minor injuries to life-threatening conditions, requiring students to perform systematic assessment and prioritized intervention. The system guides students through proper protocols while visualizing physiological responses to their actions in real-time. Students can practice specific techniques including CPR, AED use, wound management, splinting, and emergency moves with immediate feedback on their effectiveness. Interactive tools demonstrate anatomical structures affected by injuries and the physiological basis for first aid techniques. Challenge scenarios increase in complexity, introducing multiple casualties, limited resources, or environmental hazards that require adaptation of standard protocols. The simulation emphasizes both technical skills and decision-making processes, teaching students to remain calm and methodical during emergencies while understanding the scientific principles underlying effective first aid.

hypothesis.description: Students will implement first aid techniques by following systematic assessment and treatment protocols. They will prioritize interventions based on injury severity and victim condition, and adapt standard procedures to various emergency scenarios while maintaining safety for both rescuers and victims.
